answer: Consider a reef-stewardship ledger. Each seat binds one surveyed coral patch and rents a hydrophone there. Each epoch it uploads raw audio with a tide timestamp; the soundscape drifts with water temperature, snapping-shrimp choruses and wherever fish wander after storms, so clips cannot be precomputed and studio audio fails the tide and species check. Peers compare low bands with neighbouring patches: two seats on one patch emit near-identical ambience; both forfeit bond. A sybil must buy real reef, hardware and dive crews swapping batteries along the horizon, under permits naming the buyer.
